verdict.rationale: Circle documents Agent Wallets that let an AI agent hold and spend USDC autonomously "within spending policies you define," with customizable spending controls and compliance guardrails. Keys are MPC-secured, wallet creation is exposed through APIs, and the CLI can create and manage wallets. However, the pack has no detail on per-agent scoped keys and does not specify what the concrete limits or policy types are. Missing for 10: documented scoped or delegated keys per agent, concrete documentation of policy types and spending limits, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, agents can hold and use wallets safely — programmatic wallet issuance for agents with scoped keys, policy controls, and documented limits on what an agent can move

citations.quote: Agent Wallets let your AI agent hold funds and transact onchain autonomously, within spending policies you define.
Use Agent wallets to hold and spend USDC and other tokens with customizable spending controls and built-in compliance guardrails.
Circle secures keys with MPC or passkeys depending on wallet product; you get APIs to create wallets, sign transactions, and authorize actions.
Create and manage wallets, transfer, swap, and bridge USDC across blockchains
